title: Multiply by $$\frac{x}{x}$$
text: To see that the two expressions are equivalent for most values of $$x$$, we multiply the right-hand side by $$\frac{x}{x}$$. This gives $$\frac{x}{x+\frac{x}{x}}=\frac{x}{x+1}$$, which is equal to the left-hand side.

title: Interpret equivalence
text: We multiplied the left-hand side by $$\frac{x}{x}$$, which is undefined when $$x=0$$, so this forces the equivalence to fail at least when $$x=0$$. So whenever both the LHS and RHS are defined, they are equivalent.
